extracted.intended_audience: teachers and students using Flipboard for classroom and school projects
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for educators and students to create, populate, and share Flipboard magazines for school projects, virtual tours, and yearbooks using mobile and desktop tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download the app
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the app from iOS or Android.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install Flipboard on your smartphone (iOS or Android) as the first step to using it for classroom projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a complete account/profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an account: Make sure you add a picture and a complete bio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tips: Tell your story. What do you like? Share your passions. A complete profile helps others understand who you are and improves credibility for your magazines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow relevant Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the app and select some of your favorite “Topics” to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are over 34,000 Topics to choose from — following topics helps feed content relevant to your project and makes it easier to find items to add to magazines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a magazine using the 'For collecting' option
rubrics_metrics.description: Navigate to your profile and choose the “For collecting” option to build a magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the app, go to the bottom and select your profile icon. You will see a “grey” box to the left just under your profile description — select it and choose 'For collecting' to create a new magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give your magazine a clear title
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a descriptive title for your collection (e.g., class yearbook, virtual tour of Asia) so collaborators and viewers immediately understand its focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add content to a magazine via the Share menu
rubrics_metrics.description: Find an article on your smartphone, select the “Share” icon, then choose the Flipboard icon and select your magazine to add the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise: 1) Find an article on Android or iOS; 2) Tap the Share icon at the bottom of the screen; 3) Navigate to the Flipboard icon and select it; 4) Choose your magazine and add the article; 5) Add a comment in the comment box and tap 'post'. Adding a comment contextualizes the item for your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install and use the Flip.it share tool on mobile
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the 'Flip.it' share tool from a device so Flipboard appears in your social shares toolbar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for the browser Share button, go to the 'more' menu, ensure the Flipboard app is installed, select 'Flipboard' from the menu — Flipboard will then appear as an option in your sharing toolbar so you can add web articles to magazines directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add the Flip.it button on desktop browsers
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the “Flip.it” button on your desktop toolbar to add web content to magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit about.flipboard.com/tools/, add the Flip.it button to your browser toolbar, click the red Flip.it button when on a page you want to save, then add the item to a magazine. You can add blogs, Instagram links, and other web content this way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage magazines for group projects and virtual tours
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a teacher, try Flipboard for group projects, virtual tours and homeschooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flipboard magazines can be used to collate resources for class assignments, organize virtual field trips, or create shared resource collections for remote learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student use-cases: yearbooks and exploratory projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Students can build virtual tours or school yearbooks with YouTube, Instagram posts, and other media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage creativity: use Flipboard to curate multimedia class projects (e.g., a virtual tour of Asia or a digital yearbook). The platform supports embedding social links and varied content types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and scalability: free and can create many magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: Joining Flipboard is free, and you can make hundreds of magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no monetary barrier to entry — educators and students can create multiple themed magazines to organize curricula, portfolios, or project modules.
